Inferred, and correctly so -- neither Linde press release names the customer. However this is a materially sounder inference than the rejected AGC/Air Liquide-Arizona flows below: (1) Linde's own releases (2021, 2026, Tier 2) document a real, specific relationship -- an on-site complex built and then expanded for 'one of the world's largest semiconductor manufacturers' at a named city (Phoenix); (2) TSMC's Fab 21 (Phoenix, operational/under construction per the fabrication layer) is the only multi-billion-dollar logic fab in Phoenix proper in this period -- Intel's Arizona fabs are in Chandler, a different city, which the inference_note correctly uses to rule Intel out. Independently, re-reading the full 2026 Linde release during this review turned up a further corroborating detail not cited in the evidence array: the same release states Linde's Taiwan joint venture (Linde LienHwa) was 'selected by the same customer' for a simultaneous Taiwan expansion -- consistent with TSMC (headquartered in Taiwan, with major Taiwan fab operations) and not with Intel (no comparable Taiwan fab footprint). This additional textual clue was not added to the entity's evidence/inference_note (out of scope for a correction), but it materially increases confidence in the existing inference. Flagged, not rejected, given the city-level and cross-market disambiguation available; flagged because the customer is still not named in either source.

Inferred, but fails the two-documented-premises bar. Air Liquide's 2026 press release (Tier 2) does not name the customer and does not even give a city within Arizona ('a global leader in advanced semiconductor nodes... in Arizona'), only that Air Liquide has an 'existing presence at the site.' Unlike the Linde Phoenix flow, there is no disambiguating fact (no city, no cross-market detail) to distinguish TSMC from Intel, both of which are expanding advanced-node fabs in Arizona in this period -- and the analyst's own inference_note admits 'TSMC Arizona and Intel Arizona both fit... could equally be.' An admitted coin-flip is not a sound inference under AGENTS.md's standard. Reject the flow; the underlying Air Liquide facility (fac:air-liquide-arizona-onsite) is kept and published on its own facts, independent of customer identity.

Rests only on co-location (Photronics runs photomask R&D in Boise, where Micron is headquartered) -- the analyst's own inference_note states Photronics' customers are anonymized in its 10-K (Customer A/B/C) and 'no document names Micron as a Photronics customer.' Co-location alone is explicitly not a publishable basis per instructions. Reject.

AGC names no customers at all -- 'adopted by several logic and memory semiconductor manufacturers' (plural, unnamed) -- and the analyst's own inference_note calls the TSMC endpoint 'illustrative,' explicitly noting it 'could equally be Samsung, Intel or memory makers.' No second documented premise narrows the field (unlike the Linde/Phoenix case). 'Illustrative' is explicitly not a publishable basis per instructions. Reject.
